messages:
Alex Chong: Heads-up: reproducible flake in the Android sample where Retrofit calls fail after a token refresh if the request body is streamed. OkHttp logs show early EOF and then a "Suppressing retry" message.
Priya Nair: which emulator / device? any pattern?
Alex Chong: emulator API 33 and physical Pixel 6s. Seems more frequent on Wi-Fi toggle + screen off. Repro steps: send ~200KB prompt with streaming RequestBody, auth expires mid-flight, refresh kicks in, then retry suppressed.
Ben Gomez: can you paste the exact okhttp debug lines?
Alex Chong: snippet:
```
D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
D/OkHttp: Content-Type: application/json
I/Network: write request body (streaming)
W/Network: connection reset by peer during write
I/Auth: refresh token start
I/Auth: refresh token done
D/OkHttp: retrying request
E/OkHttp: retry suppressed: non-repeatable request body
E/SDK: request failed: java.io.EOFException: unexpected end of stream
```
Priya Nair: ok that's classic non-repeatable body behavior. Interceptors run in chain on the same Call; once you call chain.proceed() with a one-shot body it's gone. Are we cloning the Call for retries or just reusing the Request?
Alex Chong: our RetryInterceptor does chain.proceed(newRequest) after refresh. No call.clone() because interceptor doesn't have Call object.
Ben Gomez: right. Interceptor API doesn't give you Call, but you can detect non-repeatable bodies and surface a clearer error or buffer. For short prompts buffering is fine. For large streams you could implement a small transparent LRU buffer up to a cap.
Priya Nair: other workaround: make the AuthInterceptor synchronous before writing the body (i.e., ensure token fresh before body is streamed). E.g., move auth refresh earlier in the chain or perform preflight auth check. But that adds latency on cold calls.
Alex Chong: tried moving AuthInterceptor to run earlier but Retrofit/OkHttp still writes body as part of proceed() so if refresh is triggered by 401 only, we still hit this.
Ben Gomez: another option: use Expect: 100-continue with chunked bodies so server responds 401 before client sends full body. But servers might not send 401 pre-100. Also Android's OkHttp historically had flaky Expect support.
Alex Chong: good to know. For the sample app I'm going to change streaming to a buffered ByteArray for <=128KB and add an onboarding note.
Priya Nair: long-term: SDK should detect "isOneShotBody" and either buffer transparently up to a configurable limit or throw a clear exception that suggests buffering or pre-auth. Add an opt-in config: OkHttpClientBuilder.allowTransparentBuffering(maxBytes).
Ben Gomez: agree. add MockWebServer test where server closes socket mid-body to assert we surface a deterministic error and that retries either succeed (with buffered) or fail cleanly with guidance.
infra-bot: created issue RD-INF-7629: "android-sdk: non-repeatable streaming body -> suppressed retry during auth refresh; add buffering opt-in and docs" and attached logs.
Alex Chong: filing a PR to sample app and onboarding docs. I'll include a small snippet to show recommended RequestBody wrapper:
```
fun repeatableRequestBody(bytes: ByteArray): RequestBody = bytes.toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
```
Priya Nair: sweet. Also add a note in Retrofit quickstart: "If you rely on automatic retry on 401, ensure request bodies are repeatable or enable SDK buffering."
Ben Gomez: let's avoid surprising users: default should be fail-fast with clear message, not implicit buffering that could OOM on low-memory devices. Make buffering opt-in.
Alex Chong: agreed. I'll leave opt-in and demos in sample app. Will add telemetry event when retry suppressed to help surface customer impact. :thumbsup:
